rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those addressed claim belief but are hypocrites who appear outwardly Muslim.
rows.anchor: zâhiren Müslüman görünüp münafık olanlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the taghut as a God-defying, satanic tyrant.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan korkmaz şeytanetkâr azgına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had been commanded to reject taghut, as stated in 2:256, yet seek its court.
rows.anchor: tâğūta küfretmeye me’mur bulunuyorlardı

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s account has a Jew and hypocrite dispute; the Jew urged the Prophet’s just judgment while the hypocrite chose bribery-prone Ka‘b b. Eşref, expecting the ruling to favor him.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olan beyanlarına göre bir münafık ile bir Yahudî münâza‘a etmişler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: After the Prophet ruled for the Jew and the hypocrite rejected it, Umar killed him; Gabriel called Umar the distinguisher of truth and falsehood, and the Prophet affirmed he was al-Faruq.
rows.anchor: Cibrîl aleyhisselâm gelip “Ömer Fâruk’tur, hak ile batılı tefrik etti” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account, taghut points to Ka‘b b. Eşref.
rows.anchor: Bu surette demek ki tâğūt Ka‘b b. Eşref’e işarettir.

rows.speaker: Şa‘bî
rows.claim: A report from al-Sha‘bi says the hypocrite also invited his opponent to a soothsayer from the Juhayna tribe for judgment.
rows.anchor: Şa‘bî’den bir rivayete göre de bu münafık hasmını Cüheyne Kabilesi’nden bir kâhine de davet etmiş

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the case concerned a slain man between Qurayza and Nadir; Muslim members sought the Prophet’s judgment, while hypocrites insisted on the soothsayer Abu Bardat al-Aslami.
rows.anchor: Süddî’nin beyânına göre de hâdise Benî Kurayza ile Benî Nadîr arasında bulunan bir maktul hakkında vâki‘olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When called to Allah’s revelation and the Messenger, hypocrites turn away and obstruct.
rows.anchor: münafıkları gördün ki senden i‘râz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a calamity caused by their own acts, they come swearing that they meant only good and reconciliation.
rows.anchor: “billâhi bizim sû’-i niyetimiz yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the degree of evil in their hearts; the Prophet should turn aside, admonish them, and speak words that penetrate.
rows.anchor: Bunlar öyle kimselerdir ki kalblerindeki fenalığın derecesini Allah bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers are sent to be obeyed by God’s permission, so obeying the Prophet is obeying God and disobeying him is rebellion against God.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e itaat Allah’ın emrine itaat, ona isyan Allah’a isyandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True belief requires making the Prophet judge disputes, feeling no inward distress at his ruling, and submitting to him completely in outward and inward obedience.
rows.anchor: aralarında çatallanmış, nizâ‘lı işlerde seni hakem yapıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ordered to kill themselves or leave their homes as repentance and release from sin, as Israelites had been, all but a few would refuse.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil’de olduğu gibi günahtan tevbe ve halâs için kendi elleriyle intihar etmeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammadan law does not impose this severe burden; it forbids self-killing in 4:29 and commands protecting oneself, homeland, and religion from danger.
rows.anchor: Kendilerini ve vatanlarını ve dinlerini müdafaa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing this submission shows insincere faith and wrongs oneself and one’s homeland.
rows.anchor: buna teslîm-i nefs etmemek, ihlâs ile mü’min olmamak, nefsine ve vatanına zulmetmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the admonitions given and to come would be good for them and strengthen their firmness in good.
rows.anchor: verilen ve verilecek olan vaaz u nasihatleri yapmış olsalardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the preceding context, he prefers reading تثبيت as firm establishment in their homeland, rather than having to leave it.
rows.anchor: Biz burada mâkabli karînesiyle şu mânayı daha muvâfık buluyoruz: Diyarlarından, vatanlarından çıkmak şöyle dursun, onda kuvvetle tesbît

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that case God would grant them a great reward from His presence.
rows.anchor: tarafımızdan kendilerine muhakkak büyük bir ecir de verirdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would guide them to a straight path, connected to obeying God and the Messenger in 4:69.
rows.anchor: onları şüphesiz bir sırât-ı müstakīme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the burhan as Muhammad himself and the clear light as the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Ey insanlar! Bakın size Rabbinizden burhan geldi, size açık bir nûr indirdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is Islam’s religion and sharia, with the following surahs explaining the completion of this guidance.
rows.anchor: “Sırât-ı Müstakīm”, din ve şerî‘at-ı İslâm’dır ve bundan sonraki sûrelerde bu hidâyetin istikmâli beyan olunacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s opening call to fear God develops through the divine proof and ends at the clear light that illuminates the straight path.
rows.anchor: sûrenin başındaki يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ [en-Nisâ 4/1] hitâbı bu burhân-ı rabbânî ile inkişaf ede ede böyle bir nûr-ı mübîne müntehî olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse returns the surah’s end to its beginning by addressing death and completing the opening rulings on property and inheritance.
rows.anchor: ölüm ile alâkadar olan ve sûrenin evvelindeki ahkâm-ı emvâl ve mirası itmam eden bir âyet ile âhiri evvele ircâ‘etmek üzere buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hostility toward a people who once barred believers from the Sacred Mosque must not lead to aggression or disrespect for sacred rites.
rows.anchor: Bir zamanlar sizi Mescid-i Haram’dan men‘ettiklerinden dolayı bir kavme olan buğz sizi kendilerine taarruz ve tecavüzünüzle günaha sokmasın

rows.speaker: İbn Kesîr ve Ebû Âmir
rows.claim: Their reading places kasra on the hamza of أَن صَدُّوكُمْ, yielding the conditional sense, if a people bar you.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr ve Ebû Âmir kıraatlerinde hemze’nin kesriyle أَن صَدُّوكُمْ okunduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should cooperate in righteousness and piety.
rows.anchor: Birr ü takvâ üzerinde yardımlaşın da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must not cooperate in sin and transgression.
rows.anchor: cürm ü ta‘addî üzerinde yardımlaşmayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must fear God and heed these commands because His punishment is severe.
rows.anchor: Ve Allah’tan korkun, bu emirlere muhalefetten hazer edin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives the Hutam b. Hind incident as the verse’s chief occasion of revelation, citing Tabari, Abu Hayyan, Ebussuud, and Qadi Shihab’s gloss.
rows.anchor: (Taberî, Ebû Hayyân, Ebussuud, Hâşiye-i Kāzî Şihâb).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hutam of Banu Dubay‘a came to Medina, claimed to be a tribal emissary, and promised that he and his companions would convert; the Prophet described his treacherous appearance on leaving.
rows.anchor: Hutam Medine’ye gelmiş, atlarını Medine hâricinde bir yere bırakmış, yalnızca huzûr-ı Resûlullah’a varmış.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving Medina, Hutam stole the residents’ grazing camels and recited a rajaz poem as he drove them away.
rows.anchor: Sonra Medine’den çıkmış, Medine ahâlisinin yayılmakta olan develerine rast gelmiş, sürmüş götürmüş ve şu recezi söyleyerek gitmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stolen camels were not recovered; the following year, in the Qada Umrah season, Hutam’s people came from Yamama with trade goods and many of those camels marked as sacrificial offerings.
rows.anchor: Ertesi sene, yani Umre-i Kazâ senesi Bekir b. Vâil huccâcı meyânında Yemâme’den çıkmış, hacca gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims sought permission to attack the arriving pilgrims, but this verse was revealed and permission was withheld.
rows.anchor: Müslümanlar karşıdan bunların geldiklerini işitince karşılayıp vurmak için Resûlullah’tan istîzân etmişler, bu âyet nâzil olmuş, müsaade buyurulmamıştır

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says that at the conquest of Mecca pagans also came to visit the Kaaba and perform umrah, and Muslims wanted to raid them; the clause about pilgrims to the Sacred House was revealed.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’in rivayetine göre Feth-i Mekke senesi müşrikler dahi Kâbe’yi ziyarete geliyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the clause recalling Hudaybiyya fits Ibn Zayd’s report better.
rows.anchor: Hudeybiye’yi ihtar eden وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمْ إلخ fıkrası da buna daha ziyade mülâyimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Qada Umrah occurred in Dhu al-Qada, the sacred-month phrase first and directly refers to that month.
rows.anchor: Umre-i Kazâ zilkadede vâki‘olduğundan şehr-i haram evvelen ve bizzat buna işaret demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the cited occasions of revelation, the prohibition on turning pilgrims away from the Sacred House initially includes pagans as well as Muslim pilgrims; their search for grace and approval is according to their own religion, as they suppose.
rows.anchor: yalnız Müslüman huccâcın değil, müşriklerin bile Kâbe’yi ziyaretten men‘edilmemelerini âmirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 9:17 and 9:28 barred pagans from approaching the Sacred Mosque from year nine AH, that general rule was abrogated and the clause remained limited to Muslim pilgrims.
rows.anchor: dokuzuncu sene-i hicriyeden sonra müşrikler Mescid-i Haram’a yaklaşmaktan men‘edildikleri zaman bu umum nesh olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of scholars hold that the sacred-month prohibition was abrogated by generalizing verses such as 2:191.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-ı ulemânın kavli de budur.

rows.speaker: some scholars
rows.claim: Some scholars hold that initiating war in a sacred month remains forbidden and that the prohibition in this clause was not abrogated.
rows.anchor: bazı ulemâ şehr-i haramda taarruzî harbin memnû‘iyeti bâkī olduğuna ve taarruzu nehy eden

rows.speaker: some scholars
rows.claim: Some scholars say the Sacred House clause never included non-Muslims, since seeking divine reward and approval marks believers; therefore the Bara’a prohibitions do not conflict with it.
rows.anchor: Müslümanların gayrısına şâmil olmadığına ve çünkü يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَٰنًۭا taleb-i sevab ve rızâ-yı ilâhî mânasıyla mü’minlerin şi‘ârında zâhir bulunduğuna

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan says there is no abrogation in Surat al-Maida.
rows.anchor: Hasan radıyallahu anh “Sûre-i Mâide’de mensuh yoktur” demiş

rows.speaker: Ebû Meysere
rows.claim: Abu Maysara is quoted as saying the surah contains eighteen obligations and no abrogation.
rows.anchor: Ebû Meysere’nin “Bu sûrede on sekiz farîza vardır ve bunda mensuh yoktur” dediği de nakledilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a prophetic hadith that Maida was among the last surahs revealed and commands making its lawful lawful and its forbidden forbidden; those who cite it favor revelation of the whole surah at the Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: سُورَةُ الْمَائِدَةِ مِنْ آخِرِ الْقُرْآنِ نـُزُولاً، فَأَحِل ُّوا حَلاَلهََا وَحَ ِّرمُوا حَرَامَهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports exegetes’ consensus that all but two verses of Maida have no abrogation, and notes the undisputed timeline: pagans were not barred from Hajj until year nine and none approached during the Prophet’s year-ten Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Mâide’nin iki âyetinden mâ‘adâsında mensuh bulunmadığı hakkında da bütün müfessirînin icmâ‘ı vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The actual disagreement is whether pagans were not barred before year nine because no prohibition had yet been issued, or whether this verse positively prohibited barring them.
rows.anchor: İşte ihtilâf bu noktadadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever view is taken, abrogation leaves the clause’s certain ruling that Muslim pilgrims may not be barred from Hajj; the Bara’a verses remain decisive against pagans.
rows.anchor: her iki surette وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ fıkrasının evvel ve âhir huccâc-ı müslimînin hacdan men‘edilmemeleri hakkındaki hükmü kat‘î ve muhkemdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute’s current legal effect is the four sacred months: without abrogation Muslims may not initiate war then; if abrogated, the months are like others for defensive or offensive war, and the old restriction is lifted.
rows.anchor: Zira bazı ulemânın dediği gibi burada nesih yoksa Müslümanlar şehr-i haram denilebilen dört ayın hiçbirinde taarruzî olarak i‘lân-ı harbe şer‘an me’zun değillerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He sides with the majority that the sacred-month restriction was abrogated.
rows.anchor: Biz de cumhur ile beraber bu re’ydeyiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse strongly emphasizes special care for safety and peace during the Hajj months.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin hac aylarında âsâyişin muhafazasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After detailing the hunting exception for pilgrims in consecration, he turns to explain the following exception, illa ma yutla.
rows.anchor: İstisnâsına dair olan bu tafsilden sonra إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ istisnâsının tafsîline gelelim
